item.title: NYT bans Photoshop 2027 for freeladers due to hidden AI metadata
item.description:
NYT bans Photoshop 2027 for freeladers due to hidden AI metadata

The New York Times is asking freelance photographers to stop using the newest version of Adobe Photoshop because the 2027 update includes AI features that may not be obvious to users.

📝 The Restriction

In an email seen by The Verge and posted on Threads, photography leaders Meaghan Looram and Josh Haner stated that the use of the new features “can result in metadata identifying photographs as AI-generated.”

The specific directive reads: “At this time, we are requiring that all contributing photographers avoid using Adobe Photoshop 2027 (release 28.0.0 and subsequent updates) when working on assignment for The Times,”

🧩 Why the Metadata Matters

Adobe has spent the past few years integrating AI tools into its creative suite. The November update cited by the Times adds several new features, including:

  • AI Assisted Editor view: A single toolbar for accessing all Photoshop AI features.
  • AI Assistant: Provides step-by-step editing instructions.
  • Prompt-based Tools: For image transformation and editing.
  • AI Upscaling Options: For image enhancement.
  • AI Recomposition: A tool that recomposes images for different canvas sizes.

It is not always clear which tools are AI-powered, and some older options like automated selection tools may now be part of the AI suite. This ambiguity means photos can end up with metadata indicating they were edited with AI.

For the New York Times, which maintains that it does not “retouch or digitally manipulate” photos but only makes minimal color adjustments, this metadata is a risk. The organization views the presence of such tags as a loss of reader trust, as they serve as a blunt description of post-production work.

⚙️ Background and Context

In August, Adobe began rolling out support for C2PA metadata across its apps, which indicates whether an image is AI-generated or edited using AI features. The Times is issuing this restriction to prevent these tags from inadvertently appearing in its published photographs.

Neither Adobe nor the New York Times immediately responded to The Verge’s request for more information on which specific Photoshop features are causing the concern.

#AdobePhotoshop #NewYorkTimes #AIMetadata #Photography #CreativeSuite #C2PA

Source: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features

item.title: Meta delays enforcement of new business terms amid publisher AI-scraping concerns
item.description:
Meta delays enforcement of new business terms amid publisher AI-scraping concerns

Meta announced a delay to the rollout of its revised business terms after worldwide publisher pushback over possible AI‑training scrapes of news sites.

🔍 Overview

  • The original effective date was October 30.
  • Enforcement has been pushed to November 20.
  • Delay is intended to give Meta time to explain what is changing and what is not.
  • Publishers warned the terms could let Meta scrape news sites for AI training.

📜 Business terms details

  • The draft terms appeared to give Meta permission to freely scrape news sites for AI training.
  • Meta later removed explicit language about “training” its products, but legal experts said the change may still allow scraping.

🗣️ Publisher and regulator response

  • The News/Media Alliance sent a letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg demanding revisions, citing “severe harm” to publishers.
  • Digital advertisers and publishers in the European Union and the United Kingdom urged regulators to block the new terms.
  • Publisher backlash worldwide prompted Meta to delay the terms entirely.

🤝 Meta’s statement

  • spokesperson Daniel Roberts told The Verge the November 20 start “allows more time for us to explain to our partners and stakeholders what’s changing and what’s not.”
  • Roberts added the delay will let Meta detail “how Meta uses web crawlers and the fact that content owners will still be able to use robots.txt to signal preferences.”

💡 Why it matters

  • Scraping news content for AI models could affect revenue and control for publishers.
  • Robots.txt remains a tool for publishers to signal crawling preferences.
  • Regulatory attention in the EU and UK highlights growing scrutiny of large platforms’ data practices.

#Meta #AI #Publishing #Regulation

Source: Meta delays new business terms after publisher pushback on AI scraping
